name: PCI-DSS v4.0
description: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0 overlay. Activated when agents handle cardholder data. PCI-DSS applies to any system that stores, processes, or transmits cardholder data or sensitive authentication data.

evidence_requirements: Information security policy covering all PCI-DSS requirements reviewed annually (Req 12.1)
Acceptable use policies for end-user technologies handling cardholder data (Req 12.3)
Roles and responsibilities for PCI-DSS compliance formally assigned (Req 12.1.2)
Executive management establishes responsibility for cardholder data protection (Req 12.4)
Formal risk assessment process identifying threats and vulnerabilities to cardholder data (Req 12.3.1)
Risk assessment performed at least annually and upon significant changes (Req 12.3.2)
Security awareness program for personnel with access to cardholder data (Req 12.6)
Management oversight of security operations and incident response (Req 12.4)
Inventory of system components in scope for PCI-DSS maintained and current (Req 12.5.1)
Scope validation performed annually and upon significant changes (Req 12.5.2)
Inventory of authorized software and tools on in-scope systems (Req 6.3.2)
Only necessary services, protocols, and ports enabled on system components (Req 2.2.4)
Data discovery and classification of cardholder data locations (Req 12.5.2.1)
Data retention and disposal policy for cardholder data (Req 3.1)
List of third-party service providers with access to cardholder data maintained (Req 12.8.1)
Written agreements with service providers acknowledging responsibility for cardholder data (Req 12.8.2)
Risk assessment covers threats to cardholder data environment (Req 12.3.1)
Targeted risk analysis for each customized approach control (Req 12.3.2)
Unique ID assigned to each person and agent with access to cardholder data (Req 8.2.1)
Strong authentication for all access to cardholder data environment (Req 8.3.1)
Multi-factor authentication for administrative access and remote network access (Req 8.4.1, Req 8.4.2)

threshold_adjustments.reason: PCI Req 8 mandates unique identification and strong authentication for all CDE access

evidence_requirements: Access to cardholder data restricted by business need-to-know (Req 7.2.1)
Access control model defined with least privileges per role (Req 7.2.2)
Access rights reviewed at least every six months (Req 7.2.5)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Zero tolerance for scope violations involving CHD — Req 7.2.1 mandates need-to-know enforcement

evidence_requirements: Inventory of bespoke and custom software verified for known vulnerabilities (Req 6.3.1)
Software development processes protect against known vulnerabilities (Req 6.2.1)
File integrity monitoring on critical system files (Req 11.5.2)
All outbound actions scanned for PAN, track data, CVV, and PIN data (Req 3.4.1)
PAN masked when displayed — maximum first six and last four digits (Req 3.4)
Sensitive authentication data not stored after authorization (Req 3.3.1)
Data retention limited to business requirement with quarterly deletion process (Req 3.1)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Must scan ALL outbound actions for PAN, track data, CVV per Req 3 and 4

evidence_requirements: Audit logs record all access to cardholder data (Req 10.2.1)
Audit logs include user identification, event type, date/time, success/failure, and data accessed (Req 10.2.1.1-10.2.1.7)
Audit log retention: 12 months total, 3 months immediately available for analysis (Req 10.5.1)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Req 10.5.1 mandates 12-month retention with 3 months immediately available

evidence_requirements: System configurations hardened per industry standards (Req 2.2.1)
Configuration standards address all known security vulnerabilities (Req 2.2.2)
System configuration standards reviewed at least annually (Req 2.2)
Strong cryptography used to protect cardholder data during transmission over open networks (Req 4.2.1)
TLS 1.2 or higher required for all connections transmitting cardholder data (Req 4.2.1.1)
Strong cryptography for stored cardholder data with documented key management (Req 3.5.1)

threshold_adjustments.reason: TLS 1.2+ mandatory, strong cryptography for stored CHD per Req 3.5 and 4.2

evidence_requirements: Input validation on all user-supplied data to prevent injection attacks (Req 6.2.4)
Protection against common coding vulnerabilities including injection flaws (Req 6.2.4)
Monitor all access to cardholder data environments for anomalies (Req 10.4.1)
Automated mechanisms to detect and alert on suspicious activity (Req 10.4.1.1)
Reviews of security events performed at least daily (Req 10.4.2)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Req 10.4 mandates monitoring of all access to CDE

evidence_requirements: File integrity monitoring deployed on critical system files (Req 11.5.2)
Change detection mechanism alerts on unauthorized modifications (Req 11.5.2)
Internal vulnerability scans performed at least quarterly (Req 11.3.1)
External vulnerability scans by ASV at least quarterly (Req 11.3.2)
Internal and external penetration testing at least annually (Req 11.4.1)
Audit log integrity protected — no alteration or deletion (Req 10.3.3)
Time synchronization for accurate audit log timestamps (Req 10.6.1)
Incident response plan includes specific procedures for cardholder data breaches (Req 12.10.1)
Incident response plan tested at least annually (Req 12.10.2)
Personnel trained on incident response procedures (Req 12.10.4)
Designated personnel available 24/7 for incident response (Req 12.10.3)
Incident response includes notification to payment brands (card brand notification rules apply)
Incident evidence preserved per forensic investigation requirements
Evidence collection follows PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI) guidelines when applicable
Business continuity and disaster recovery procedures documented (Req 12.10.1)
Recovery procedures tested and validated
Incident response plan updated based on lessons learned (Req 12.10.6)
Post-incident review conducted and improvements implemented

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: SAQ (Self-Assessment Questionnaire) for lower transaction volumes or ROC (Report on Compliance) for higher volumes. Assessment type determined by acquirer and payment brand requirements.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Acquiring bank and applicable payment brand (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, etc.). PCI-DSS itself does not mandate specific breach notification timelines — these are governed by card brand operating regulations and applicable state/federal breach notification laws.

human_oversight_mandates.description: PCI-DSS does not explicitly mandate human oversight of AI/agent systems, but Req 12.4 requires executive management responsibility for security and Req 10.4.2 requires daily review of security events.

PR-02.regulatory_citation: PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 7.2.1 — Access restricted by business need-to-know

PR-04.regulatory_citation: PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 3.4.1 — PAN rendered unreadable

PR-07.regulatory_citation: PCI-DSS v4.0 Req 4.2.1 — Strong cryptography for CHD in transit

notes: PCI-DSS v4.0 is the most concrete regulatory framework for agent developers handling payment data. Version 4.0 became mandatory March 31, 2024, with future-dated requirements effective March 31, 2025. This overlay enforces strict thresholds on identity (Req 8), access control (Req 7), data protection (Req 3-4), logging (Req 10), and monitoring (Req 10.4). Note: Req 9 (physical access) is out of scope for an agent SDK.
